descriptions.azteca: The only stadium ever to host two World Cup finals (1970 and 1986) — and in 2026 the first to stage matches at a third tournament. Sitting 2,200 m above sea level, its thin air is a famous test for visiting teams.
descriptions.akron: Home of Chivas Guadalajara, rising out of the landscape like a volcano with its grass-covered outer slope. One of three Mexican venues for 2026.
descriptions.bbva: Nicknamed 'El Gigante de Acero' (the Steel Giant), with a sweeping open view of the Cerro de la Silla mountain behind the south stand.
descriptions.metlife: The stage for the 2026 World Cup final on July 19. Shared home of the NFL's Giants and Jets, and the largest stadium of the tournament.
descriptions.gillette: Home of the New England Patriots and Revolution, about 35 km south-west of Boston. Its lighthouse tower is a New England landmark.
descriptions.lincoln: Philadelphia's football cathedral, home of the NFL's Eagles, known for one of the loudest crowds in American sport.
descriptions.mercedes: Atlanta's architectural showpiece with a pinwheel roof that opens like a camera aperture. Home of Atlanta United, who set MLS attendance records here.
descriptions.hardrock: Miami's open-air arena, renovated with a canopy that shades the stands while leaving the pitch under the Florida sun. Also hosts the F1 Miami Grand Prix and the Miami Open.
descriptions.att: The Dallas Cowboys' colossus in Arlington — one of the world's largest domed stadiums, famous for its centre-hung video board nearly 50 m wide.
descriptions.nrg: Houston's retractable-roof stadium, the first NFL venue with one. Hosted two Super Bowls and the 2024 Copa América.
descriptions.arrowhead: One of the loudest stadiums on earth — Kansas City Chiefs fans set the world crowd-noise record here at 142.2 dB in 2014.
descriptions.sofi: The most expensive stadium ever built (~$5 bn), opened in 2020 in Inglewood. Its translucent roof and double-sided Infinity Screen set a new benchmark.
descriptions.levis: The San Francisco 49ers' high-tech home in the heart of Silicon Valley, hosting its second World Cup-era showpiece after Super Bowl 50.
descriptions.lumen: Seattle's cauldron, engineered to trap crowd noise — Sounders and Seahawks fans make it one of the most intimidating venues in North America.
descriptions.bmo: Toronto's lakeside football ground, home of Toronto FC, expanded to around 45,000 seats for the World Cup — Canada's men play their 2026 group games here.
descriptions.bcplace: Downtown Vancouver's retractable-roof arena, host of the 2010 Winter Olympics ceremonies and the 2015 Women's World Cup final.
